children: When asked if AI financing will be risk-free, Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco President Mary Daly said it will be a transformative technology that's useful to invest in.
Daly was speaking before the Economic Policy in the Age of AI Policy Forum hosted by the Stanford Institute for Economic Policy Research.
The private sector investors and market participants questioning AI financing creating more opportunity for an orderly valuation to right-size returns with expectations, she said.
"And so, this is somewhat good news. But the second part of the story is that the underlying value isn't being eroded," she noted.
"And you put those two things together, and that single belief that this will be a transformative technology, it's useful to invest in," said the FOMC's alternate voting member.
"And that is contributing to some of the projections you see for growth and some of our own sense, my own sense that growth will continue. There's not a risk to growth here," she added.
On AI-related inflation, Daly said, "There is no doubt that AI is fueling price pressures." However, right now headline inflation is being driven by other variables, not the AI goods.

"The price of technology equipment is not just narrowly focused on those going up for data centers. It's going up everywhere. And so certainly, firms are feeling that cost. The question is, are those indirect costs rising so sufficiently that we're going to see it in overall inflation," Daly asked.

title: AI is useful to invest in, says San Francisco Fed's Daly when asked if AI financing is risk-free
